records.subject: Exposure of nickel-aluminum bronze to a time-dependent magnetic field
records.object: Anodic current density of nickel-aluminum bronze
records.quote: Nickel-aluminum bronze (NAB) was anodically polarized in a solution of 3.5 wt% NaCl and exposed to a time-dependent magnetic field (TDMF) with an amplitude of 180 mT.
context_quotes: The effect of a TDMF on the anodic behavior of NAB has been investigated as a function TDMF frequency (0 Hz to150 Hz) and the anodic polarization potential (-180 mV(Ag/AgCl) to -25 mV(Ag/AgCl)).
The results show that the anodic current density at a fixed, anodic potential increases when NAB is exposed to a TDMF.
modality_evidence: Nickel-aluminum bronze (NAB) was anodically polarized in a solution of 3.5 wt% NaCl and exposed to a time-dependent magnetic field (TDMF) with an amplitude of 180 mT.
The effect of a TDMF on the anodic behavior of NAB has been investigated as a function TDMF frequency (0 Hz to150 Hz) and the anodic polarization potential (-180 mV(Ag/AgCl) to -25 mV(Ag/AgCl)).
records.conditions: Fixed anodic potential; 3.5 wt% NaCl; field amplitude 180 mT; investigated frequencies 0–150 Hz and potentials −180 to −25 mV versus Ag/AgCl

records.subject: Increasing aqueous LiBr concentration
records.object: Iron corrosion region extending to lower potentials
records.quote: Potential-pH diagrams of iron are developed in aqueous LiBr solutions with concentrations of 400 g/L, 700 g/L, 850 g/L, and 992 g/L LiBr at 25 degrees C, which are common concentrations in different parts of absorption machines.
context_quotes: Comparison of the potential-pH diagrams of iron in the absence and the presence of concentrated aqueous LiBr solutions shows that the corrosion area at acid, neutral, and weak alkaline pH extends to lower potentials and higher pH values with the increase of LiBr concentration, as a result of formation of the aqueous species FeBr2(aq) and FeBr3(aq) and destabilization of the solid species Fe, Fe(OH)(2)(s), Fe3O4, and Fe2O3.
records.conditions: Potential–pH diagram comparison at 25 °C; LiBr concentrations 400, 700, 850 and 992 g/L and absence of LiBr; acidic, neutral and weakly alkaline pH
